outcome: Complications of non-obstetric surgery during pregnancy
Intrauterine growth restriction/small for gestational age
cohort: Pregnant women who underwent non-obstetric surgery at a single institution in Australia between 2009 and 2018
finding: Non-obstetric surgery during pregnancy was associated with a 19% perinatal complication rate, which is comparable to the general population.
mod_finding: Women who underwent open intra-abdominal surgery had a significantly higher cesarean delivery rate compared to those who had laparoscopic surgery (67% vs. 24%, p=0.04).
